newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar stays firm, March abandons $300.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar stays firm, March abandons $300.

text.p: London's spot March white sugar contract faltered after its earlier assault on resistance at $300 and slipped back to drift just above opening levels in thin Wednesday activity, traders said.

After one small trade house cross suddenly pushed March up $2.00 to touch $300.00 around midday, widening the position's price range to $3.60, the spot value soon wandered lower and settled back into a comfortable drift.
"It's mundane," said one trader, referring to the day's activity but also noting light interest to trade the March/May spread.
At 1646 GMT March was up 80 cents at $298.00 and May up 40 cents at $297.50. Volume amounted to 690 lots.

Traders said they were watching the spot white premium and also 10.40 cents/lb as a resistance point for New York's March contract, saying that London could be dragged higher if buy stops were triggered on the raws. Trading was very thin on the Paris market where just 270 lots changed hands. March and May were both up 50 cents and both stood at $297.50.
